title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: The version catalog stops being a dead end
summary: Ctrl+click worked into gradle/libs.versions.toml and never out of it. Now a version.ref lands on its declaration, and an alias lands on the build files that use it.

highlights.title: A version.ref jumps to its declaration
highlights.description: Ctrl+click on the target of a version.ref lands on the line of the versions table that declares it, inside the same file.

highlights.title: An alias jumps to the build files that use it
highlights.description: Ctrl+click on an alias opens its usages, and Shift+F12 lists them. Accessors are matched the way Gradle resolves them, segment by segment.

sections.heading: Added
bullets: A key of the versions table jumps to the entries that pin their version on it, the question worth asking before changing a number.
Measured on a project of 5088 files: 171 of the 176 aliases resolve to at least one usage, and the five that do not are absent from every build file.
